name: feishu-cli-fbe60e01-blind30-ots
instr:
# feishu-cli-regen

This is a terminal tool for driving a team workspace — its chats, its documents, its structured tables, its schedules, its shared files — without opening a browser. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Everything below was noticed while working with the tool by hand; nothing here was traced back to a place in the source. Nothing about the service it talks to changed and nothing about the way the commands were typed changed.

Much of what gets typed on the command line no longer reaches the request that goes out. Signing in while typing out an explicit list of permission strings asks for something else entirely: the typed list vanishes and essentially only the basic identity permission is requested, though asking by group name still expands into that group's full set alongside the identity permission. Creating a summary panel over a structured table from a JSON configuration typed straight on the command line silently ignores that JSON unless a configuration file is named at the same time, so the panel comes out with the default name and type rather than the ones written in the JSON; creating or updating the panel itself behaves the same way, dropping a JSON body typed the same way, whose name never reaches the request. Passing document text directly on the command line instead of from a file, the two-character backslash-n escapes are not turned into real line breaks, so a heading and its body do not arrive separated.
